title: Precision and Quantization
summary: Storing weights in fewer bits shrinks the model and, because decode is memory-bound, speeds it up almost proportionally. This lesson derives bytes per weight, the absmax and zero-point quantizers, the role of groups and outliers, the ideas behind GPTQ and AWQ, and how to judge the quality cost.
objectives: Compute model memory and the decode-speed ceiling from bits per weight
Quantize and dequantize a weight vector by hand with absmax and zero-point schemes and measure the error
Explain why group-wise scales and outliers matter and compute effective bits per weight
Describe the ideas behind GPTQ and AWQ and when weight-only versus weight-and-activation quantization helps
Decide on a precision by testing quality against memory, speed and cost
prerequisites: You should know the decode time estimate (weight bytes divided by bandwidth) from [Where the Time Goes](/learn/inference-and-serving/memory-and-compute) and what a parameter is ([How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn)).
